ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Gathering of the Whakapapa / Tā Moko

fullPassage:
Gathering of the Whakapapa

The phone rang, and it was my dad calling from my hometown, Waituhi.
"Can you take a week off?" he asked. "Your Nani Tama wants you here."
"But Dad!" I answered. "My boss won't let me take any more time off."
The phone went silent, and then I heard my grandfather say faintly, "I need your help, Grandson. I must go to Murupara to finish the whakapapa. Drive me there. Hurry, I may not have much time."
I just knew I had no choice. "All right, Nani," I replied with a sigh. "I'll come."

For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past. In only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina.
Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands. He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the present once more. The village went quiet and listened to his chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy, searching back across the centuries. Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the middle of the chant. The village waited in worried silence until the next name burst out of his mouth. It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to drive him to Murupara to finish his work.

When I arrived at Auntie's place, I was shocked to see how thin Nani Tama was.
"Look, Nani," I said. "I'm not taking you anywhere. You could die on me!"
Nani looked at me in anger.
"You want me to die here in this room? Looking at these four walls? When the whakapapa is not yet finished?"
The old man held on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow, painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could not help but carry him to the car, and we set off with Auntie.

We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had taught Auntie. They sang together, lifting up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky.

Just before noon, we arrived at a small town called Murupara.
"Where do we go now?" I asked Nani.
He did not reply, but he was searching inside himself, staring at the small houses. Then, at a street corner, he told us to turn. After turning the corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a house. He welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in his eyes, I saw the message, "We must hurry."

Now that day seems like a dream to me. I remember the two old men sitting at the table and the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked. All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. I felt as if people from the past were looking over the shoulders of the two old men to see if the work was correct.
Finally, they stopped. It was done. After a moment of silence, the old man whispered to Nani, "Goodbye, friend." Crying, they pressed their noses together to say goodbye.

It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because our grandfather had saved our past for us.
Our Nani Tama smiled again. His smile grew tired.
He sighed. "At last, I may go now."
Then, he closed his eyes.
"No, Dad!" Auntie Hiraina cried.
The sun burst across the hills.

Deep Learning: Tā Moko: A Record of an Individual's Path

Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual's journey from their past to their present. Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person's whakapapa (genealogy), social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire faces, while women have it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage throughout their lives. Although tā moko is less common these days, it is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage for the next generation.

questions.passage: The phone rang, and it was my dad ①<u>calling</u> from my hometown, Waituhi. The phone went silent, and then I heard my grandfather ②<u>say</u> faintly, "I need your help, Grandson." I just knew I had no choice. "All right, Nani," I replied with a sigh. "I'll ③<u>came</u>." For some time, my grandfather had been busy ④<u>writing</u> down the village genealogy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: "나니, 알겠어요. 갈게요(I'll come)."
det.analysis: ✅ ③ came → come: 'will + 동사원형' 구조. will 뒤에 과거형 came은 불가. ❌ ① calling: 'it was my dad calling'에서 현재분사 보어 적절. ❌ ② say: 'heard + 목적어 + 동사원형' 지각동사 구문 적절. ❌ ④ writing: 'be busy + -ing(~하느라 바쁘다)' 적절.
det.tip: will/shall + 동사원형: I'll come(올 것이다). be busy -ing: ~하느라 바쁘다.

questions.passage: The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, ①<u>which</u> ran through the house and destroyed our past. Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter. Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands. He chanted the names of the ancestors, ②<u>joining</u> the past to the present once more. The village went quiet and ③<u>listened</u> to his chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy, ④<u>searched</u> back across the centuries.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 그의 목소리는 수세기를 거슬러 찾아 올라갔다(searching).
det.analysis: ✅ ④ searched → searching: 분사구문. 'His voice traveled ~, searching back ~'에서 동시동작의 현재분사가 필요. ❌ ① which: 선행사 'the fire'를 수식하는 계속적 관계대명사 적절. ❌ ② joining: 동시동작 분사구문 적절. ❌ ③ listened: 'went quiet and listened'에서 and로 연결된 과거형 적절.
det.tip: 분사구문(동시동작): 주어 + 동사 ~, V-ing ~. traveled ~ , searching ~ (여행하며 ~ 찾으며).

questions.passage: When I arrived at Auntie's place, I was shocked ①<u>to see</u> how thin Nani Tama was. The old man held on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow, painful step hurt him, but he tried ②<u>to walk</u>. I could not help but ③<u>carry</u> him to the car, and we ④<u>set up</u> with Auntie.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 이모와 함께 출발했다(set off).
det.analysis: ✅ ④ set up → set off: 'set off'는 '출발하다', 'set up'은 '설치하다'. 차를 타고 출발하는 맥락에서 set off가 적절. ❌ ① to see: 감정의 원인을 나타내는 to부정사 적절. ❌ ② to walk: 'tried to walk(걸으려 노력했다)' 적절. ❌ ③ carry: 'could not help but + 동사원형' 구문 적절.
det.tip: set off = 출발하다 = depart. set up = 설치하다, 세우다. could not help but + 동사원형 = ~하지 않을 수 없다.

questions.passage: Now that day seems like a dream to me. I remember the two old men ①<u>sitting</u> at the table and the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked. All through the quiet afternoon, they recalled ②<u>missing</u> names. I felt as if people from the past ③<u>are</u> looking over the shoulders of the two old men. After a moment of silence, the old man whispered to Nani, "Goodbye, friend." ④<u>Crying</u>, they pressed their noses together to say goodbye.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 과거의 사람들이 두 노인의 어깨 너머로 보고 있는 것 같았다(were looking).
det.analysis: ✅ ③ are → were: 'as if + 가정법 과거(were)'. 주절이 과거(felt)이므로 as if 절도 과거. ❌ ① sitting: 'remember + 목적어 + V-ing(~하는 것을 기억하다)' 적절. ❌ ② missing: '빠진(형용사적 현재분사)' 적절. ❌ ④ Crying: 분사구문(동시동작) 적절.
det.tip: as if + 가정법 과거: 주절 과거 → as if S + 과거동사(were). felt as if ~ were ~.

questions.passage: The phone went silent, and then I heard my grandfather say faintly, "I need your help, Grandson. I must go to Murupara to finish the whakapapa. Hurry, I may not have much time." I just knew I had no __________. "All right, Nani," I replied with a sigh. "I'll come."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나는 선택의 여지가 없다는 것을 알았다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②choice(선택): 'had no choice(선택의 여지가 없다)'. 할아버지의 간절한 부탁에 거절할 수 없는 상황. ❌ ①chance(기회): 기회가 아니라 선택의 문제. ❌ ③reason(이유): 이유가 없는 게 아니라 선택지가 없음. ❌ ④courage(용기): 용기의 문제가 아님.
det.tip: have no choice = 선택의 여지가 없다. reply with a sigh = 한숨을 쉬며 대답하다.

questions.passage: Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person's whakapapa, social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most ①<u>sacred</u> part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are added to their tattoos to ②<u>conceal</u> their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a ③<u>rite</u> of passage throughout their lives. It is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to ④<u>preserve</u> their traditions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나이가 들수록 문신에 더 많은 선과 모양이 추가되어 삶의 경험을 반영한다(reflect). conceal(숨기다)은 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ② conceal(숨기다): 원문은 reflect(반영하다). 문신은 삶의 경험을 드러내는 것이지 숨기는 것이 아님. ❌ ① sacred(신성한): 원문 그대로 적절. ❌ ③ rite(의식): rite of passage(통과 의례) 원문 그대로. ❌ ④ preserve(보존하다): 원문 그대로 적절.
det.tip: reflect(반영하다) ↔ conceal(숨기다). rite of passage: 통과 의례.

questions.passage: For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"화재로 인해 할아버지의 집에 있던 족보가 소실되었다."

det.korean: 화재가 집을 관통하며 과거를 파괴했다 = 족보가 소실됨. 일치(T).
det.analysis: ✅ T: 원문에 'the fire ran through the house and destroyed our past'라고 명시. 족보가 집에 있었고 화재로 파괴됨.
det.tip: destroy: 파괴하다. run through: ~을 관통하다.

questions.passage: It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to drive him to Murupara to finish his work.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"나니 타마는 2년 만에 족보를 완전히 완성했다."

det.korean: 2년에 걸쳐 대부분 모았지만 여전히 빈 이름이 있었다. 불일치(F).
det.analysis: ✅ F: 원문은 'gather most of the whakapapa'이지 전부가 아님. 'still missing names'이 남아 있었으므로 '완전히 완성'은 거짓.
det.tip: most of ≠ all of. fill in: 빈칸을 채우다.

questions.passage: Men typically wear tā moko over their entire faces, while women have it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are added.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"마오리족 남성과 여성은 동일한 위치에 타 모코를 새긴다."

det.korean: 남성은 얼굴 전체, 여성은 입술과 턱에 새긴다. 불일치(F).
det.analysis: ✅ F: 원문에서 남성은 'entire faces', 여성은 'lips and chins'로 위치가 다름.
det.tip: typically: 일반적으로. entire: 전체의. chin: 턱.

questions.passage: We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had taught Auntie. They sang together, lifting up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky. Just before noon, we arrived at a small town called Murupara. He did not reply, but he was __________, staring at the small houses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그는 대답하지 않고 작은 집들을 응시하며 내면을 탐색하고 있었다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④searching inside himself: 원문 표현. 기억 속에서 길을 찾고 있었다. ❌ ①falling asleep: 목적지 도착 직후 잠드는 것은 부적절. ❌ ②talking to Auntie: 대답하지 않았다고 했으므로 모순. ❌ ③looking at the map: 지도 언급 없음. 기억에 의존.
det.tip: search inside himself = 내면/기억 속을 탐색하다. stare at = ~을 응시하다.

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual's journey from their past to their present. Each curved line and pattern represents a person's whakapapa, social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: all Maori people have identical tattoos
no two tā moko designs look the same
tā moko is purely a decorative art form
tattooing is now banned in Maori culture

det.korean: 이것이 두 개의 타 모코 디자인이 같지 않은 이유를 설명한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②no two tā moko designs look the same: 각 사람의 족보, 사회적 지위, 업적이 다르므로 문신도 모두 다르다. ❌ ①identical tattoos: 모든 디자인이 다르다는 내용과 정반대. ❌ ③purely decorative: '장식적일 뿐만 아니라(not only decorative but also)'이므로 거짓. ❌ ④now banned: 여전히 실행된다고 했으므로 거짓.
det.tip: no two ~ look the same = 어떤 두 ~도 같지 않다. accomplishment: 업적.

questions.passage: The phone rang, and it was my dad calling from my hometown, Waituhi. "Can you take a week off?" he asked. The phone went silent, and then I heard my grandfather say faintly, "I need your help, Grandson. I must go to Murupara to finish the whakapapa. Drive me there. Hurry, I may not have much time." I just knew I had no choice.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 할아버지는 족보를 완성하기 위해 무루파라에 가야 했다.
화자의 아버지가 무루파라까지 운전해 주겠다고 했다.

det.korean: 할아버지는 족보를 완성하기 위해 무루파라에 가야 했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: 원문 'I must go to Murupara to finish the whakapapa'와 일치. ❌ ①: 아버지가 전화한 후 할아버지가 끼어들었지, 할아버지가 직접 전 것이 아님. ❌ ②: 'replied with a sigh'로 마지못해 동의. ❌ ④: 화자(손자)에게 운전해 달라고 함.
det.tip: faintly: 희미하게. finish the whakapapa: 족보를 완성하다.

questions.passage: After turning the corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a house. He welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in his eyes, I saw the message, "We must hurry." All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled missing names. Finally, they stopped. It was done. After a moment of silence, the old man whispered to Nani, "Goodbye, friend." Crying, they pressed their noses together to say goodbye.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 무루파라의 노인이 나니 타마를 부드러운 미소로 맞이했다.
두 노인은 오후 내내 저녁까지 빠진 이름을 회상했다.
작업이 끝난 후 두 노인은 코를 맞대며 작별 인사를 했다.
무루파라의 노인이 나니 타마와 함께 마을로 돌아왔다.

det.korean: 무루파라의 노인이 함께 돌아왔다는 내용은 원문에 없다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④: 원문에서 두 노인은 무루파라에서 작별 인사를 나눈 후 헤어짐. 함께 돌아왔다는 언급 없음. ❌ ①: 'welcomed with a gentle smile' 일치. ❌ ②: 'All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening' 일치. ❌ ③: 'pressed their noses together to say goodbye' 일치.
det.tip: press noses together = 코를 맞대다 (마오리식 인사/작별). whisper: 속삭이다.

questions.passage: It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. (A) All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. (B) Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. (C) Our hearts were full because our grandfather has saved our past for us. (D) Our Nani Tama smiled again.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 어법상 틀린 문장은?

det.korean: (C) has saved → had saved: 과거보다 이전의 행위이므로 과거완료.
det.analysis: ✅ (C): 'were full'이 과거이므로, 그 이유가 되는 행위(save)는 대과거 = 과거완료 had saved. ❌ (A): 과거 시제 적절. ❌ (B): 분사구문 적절. ❌ (D): 과거 시제 적절.
det.tip: 대과거(past perfect): 과거의 시점보다 더 이전에 완료된 행위 → had + p.p.

questions.passage: Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands. He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the present once more. The village went quiet and listened to his chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy, searching back across the centuries.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

나니는 과거의 잔해에서 벗어날 방법을 찾기 위해 떨리는 손으로 족보를 다시 쓰기 시작했다. 그는 조상들의 이름을 외우며 과거를 현재에 다시 연결했다. 마을은 조용해졌고 그의 __________에 귀를 기울였다.

det.korean: 마을은 그의 구송(chanting)에 귀를 기울였다.
det.analysis: ✅ chanting: 원문 'listened to his chanting'에서 직접 찾을 수 있음.
det.tip: chanting: 구송, 읊조림. chant(동사) → chanting(명사/동명사).

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a __________ (culture) significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual's journey from their past to their present.

questions.passage: For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past. Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter. Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands. He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the present once more. It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing names he needed to fill in.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 화재로 잃은 마을 족보를 되살리려는 할아버지의 노력
마오리족의 전통적인 주거 양식과 화재 예방
조상의 이름을 외우는 마오리족의 종교 의식
자연재해 후 마을 공동체의 재건 과정

det.korean: 이 글의 핵심은 화재로 잃은 족보를 되살리려는 할아버지의 노력이다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①: 화재 → 절망 → 떨리는 손으로 재작성 → 2년간 노력의 서사. ❌ ②: 주거 양식이나 화재 예방은 주제 아님. ❌ ③: 종교 의식이 아니라 가족 역사 기록. ❌ ④: 마을 재건이 아니라 족보 복원.
det.tip: whakapapa(족보) 복원이 글의 중심 사건. in despair: 절망 속에.

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual's journey from their past to their present. Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person's whakapapa (genealogy), social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage throughout their lives. Although tā moko is less common these days, it is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage for the next generation.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 타 모코는 마오리족의 미적 감각을 보여주는 장식 예술이다.
타 모코는 개인의 정체성과 역사를 담은 상징적인 문화 유산이다.
타 모코는 현대 사회에서 점차 사라지고 있는 관행이다.
마오리족은 얼굴에만 문신을 새기는 유일한 민족이다.

det.korean: 이 글의 요지는 타 모코가 개인의 정체성과 역사를 담은 상징적인 문화 유산이라는 것이다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 'not only decorative but also symbolic', 족보+사회적 지위+업적 반영, 통과 의례, 보존 노력까지 포괄. ❌ ①: '장식적일 뿐만 아니라'이므로 장식만 강조하면 부분적. ❌ ③: less common이지만 still practiced이므로 사라진다는 것은 과장. ❌ ④: '유일한 민족'이라는 언급 없음.
det.tip: not only A but also B = A뿐만 아니라 B도. heritage: 유산. rite of passage: 통과 의례.

questions.passage: It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because our grandfather had saved our past for us.
questions.stem:
위 글을 참고하여 다음 빈칸을 영어로 완성하시오.

마을 사람들이 우리를 기다리고 있었고, 나니 타마는 미소 지으며 족보를 들어 올려 마을에 바쳤다. 할아버지가 우리의 과거를 구해주셨기 때문에 우리의 마음은 __________.

det.korean: 우리의 마음은 벅찼다(full).
det.analysis: ✅ full: 원문 'Our hearts were full'. 감동과 감사로 마음이 가득 찬 상태.
det.tip: Our hearts were full = 마음이 벅찼다/가득 찼다. offer: 바치다.
